claim_verdicts.evidence: Execution: in that same run fd 1 and fd 2 resolved to one destination while fd 0 differed, and the two are separately redirectable — `ls <missing> > out.txt` left `ls: cannot access '...': No such file or directory` on the terminal with out.txt at 0 bytes, while `ls <missing> 2> errors.txt` printed nothing and put that same line in the file. claim_verdicts.evidence:
Execution: `printf 'a
b
a
' | uniq -c` printed `1 a`, `1 b`, `1 a` — the two equal lines are not collapsed because they are not adjacent. With `sort` inserted first the same input gives `2 a`, `1 b`. Each written line carries the size of the run it replaced, which is why `sort` has to come first for a count over a whole file.
claim_verdicts.source: execution (host shell, GNU coreutils)

claim_verdicts.evidence:
Execution: `printf '2
10
3
' | sort -rn` printed 10, 3, 2 while `sort -r` alone printed 3, 2, 10 — `-n` compares the leading number as a number and `-r` reverses. On the lesson's own chain, `sort letters.txt | uniq -c | sort -rn` put `      3 a` above `      2 b` above `      1 c`.
claim_verdicts.source: execution (host shell, GNU coreutils)

claim_verdicts.evidence:
Execution, one file in a scratch folder, three steps: `printf 'one
two
' > t.txt`; then `printf 'x
' > t.txt`, after which the file held `x` alone — both earlier lines were gone before the write; then `printf 'y
' >> t.txt`, after which it held `x` then `y`. `>` truncates first, `>>` adds after what is already there.
claim_verdicts.source: execution (host shell)

claim_verdicts.evidence: Execution: `ls <missing> > out.txt` printed `ls: cannot access '...': No such file or directory` on the terminal and left out.txt at 0 bytes, so `>` moved standard output only; `ls <missing> 2> errors.txt` printed nothing and put that line in the file. `echo err 2> dup.txt >&2` wrote `err` into dup.txt — `>&2` points a stream at whatever descriptor 2 currently is, so the `2` in `2>` and in `>&2` names the same descriptor.
claim_verdicts.source: execution (host shell)

claim_verdicts.evidence: Execution: `echo err 2> dup.txt >&2` put `err` in dup.txt and nothing on the terminal — with fd 2 already pointing at the file, `>&2` made that echo write there instead of to standard output. (`bash -c '...' 2>/dev/null` was not runnable in this session; the file form settles the same point.)
claim_verdicts.source: execution (host shell)

claim_verdicts.evidence: Execution: after `log=/repo/lab/app.log`, `echo "double: $log"` printed `double: /repo/lab/app.log`, while `echo 'single: $log'` printed `single: $log` — inside single quotes there is no expansion, so "in quotes" without saying which quotes is a missing condition. claim_verdicts.suggested_text: An assignment `name=value` gives a value a name in the shell, and `$name` inside double quotes is replaced by that value wherever it is written; inside single quotes it is not.
